before.name: Prakash Karat
before.note: Observed on 11 April 2005: People's Democracy of 17 April 2005 reports that at the public meeting in New Delhi on April 11 concluding the 18th Congress Surjeet 'was escorted to the podium by the newly-elected general secretary, Prakash Karat' (Internet Archive capture of the party organ).
before.uncertainty: No start: the same issue says he 'has been unanimously elected' by the new Central Committee without a day. No end: he inaugurated the 21st Congress as 'general secretary of the CPI(M)' on 14 April 2015 and was 'the outgoing general secretary' on 19 April 2015; no record states the day he left the office, and his successor's election or observation is not used as his end. His interim coordinatorship of 2024-2025 is claims only and is not this office.

reviewed.name: Prakash Karat
reviewed.note: Observed on 10 September 2011: the party release identifies Karat as General Secretary while publishing his note for the National Integration Council meeting in New Delhi that day. Earlier party-office styling remains in the claims; this is a conservative choice of evidence for the structured observation.
reviewed.uncertainty: No start established: the 2005 Central Committee election report gives no day of assumption. The newly elected descriptions at the 2005 and 2012 rallies remain claims and are not selected as holder dates in this amendment; their office styling is not rejected as false. No stated end: the April 2015 inaugural and outgoing-office descriptions do not give the day Karat left office, and a successor election supplies no such end. His 2024-2025 interim coordinatorship is a separate arrangement, not this office. The selected 2011 text survives here as a current REST representation, not an independently retrieved contemporary capture.

before.name: Sitaram Yechury
before.note: Observed on 19 April 2015: People's Democracy of 26 April 2015 reports that at the public meeting concluding the 21st Congress on April 19 the 'Newly elected general secretary, Sitaram Yechury, addressing the gathering' spoke (Internet Archive capture of the party organ). Until 12 September 2024: the Polit Bureau's statement records 'the passing away of Comrade Sitaram Yechury, General Secretary of the Party on September 12, 2024'.
before.uncertainty: No start: the 21st Congress election of 19 April 2015 names nobody, the Polit Bureau list of the same issue has no day, and no record states the day he assumed the office. His re-elections at the 22nd (22 April 2018) and 23rd (10 April 2022) Congresses are claims, not new starts. The end is the day of death stated with the office in the party's own statement, the rule applied in CLAUDE-C01-34.

reviewed.name: Sitaram Yechury
reviewed.note: Observed on 6 May 2015: Yechury signs a letter of that date as General Secretary; the party release reproducing it is dated 8 May. Earlier party-office styling remains in the claims. The unchanged end, 12 September 2024, is the death date recorded with his office in the Polit Bureau statement.
reviewed.uncertainty: No start established: the April 2015 election claim names nobody, the Polit Bureau list has no day, and none of these records states when Yechury assumed office. The newly elected rally description of 19 April remains evidence but is not the selected holder date in this amendment; this is not a finding that its office styling was false. His 2018 and 2022 re-elections do not create new starts. The end remains the death date explicitly recorded with the office. The selected letter survives here as a current REST representation, not an independently retrieved contemporary capture.

decision_limit: Earlier source styling remains true as an attributed source observation. Choosing later explicit office statements does not establish a new historical assumption date, restore a continuous tenure, or prohibit another independently supported observation on an election day.
